conclusion: The PROVEN/DEAD split is correct for 94 of 100 boundaries and wrong for 5, with 1 undecidable statically.
The resolver's 82 was an under-estimate produced by path-finding gaps (object-literal factories, port-typed dependency objects, accessor-returned runtimes), not by real unreachability.

callersFor()'s material defect is its CALLER LIST: 748 entries collapse to 165 qualified ones. That is an evidence-quality defect: any disposition, coverage argument or rationale that cited a recorded caller may be citing an unrelated call site.

Affected evidence already closed in this round: C1 and C5 both cited recorded callers that are confirmed collisions (C1's original relation reached the canonical-knowledge repository's own commit; C5's reached the V2 repository); C3's original relation reached the knowledge-draft repository. All three were resolved by MINIMAL_PROOF or REBIND rather than by trusting the recorded caller, so the evidence outcome is unaffected.
